title: Photo number four
hook: You're tagged in a photo you hate. 40 likes and counting.

n1.text: Arjun has posted ten photos from the college fest. In the fourth one you're mid-bite, eyes half shut, tagged. Forty likes. The comments are all 😂. You hate it.

choices.label: Quietly untag yourself
choices.consequence: The tag is gone. The photo is still up. Someone types your name in the comments anyway.
choices.expert_note: Untagging is a real tool, and it's yours to use. It doesn't tell Arjun anything, though.

choices.label: DM him: "Bro, please take the 4th one down. I really don't like it."
choices.consequence: Arjun: lol you look fine. it's funny
choices.expert_note: A direct ask is fair. "You look fine" answers a question you didn't ask. This is about whether you're okay with it being up.

choices.label: Comment: "delete this 😭"
choices.consequence:
It gets six likes.
Arjun: never
The joke just made the photo bigger.
choices.expert_note: Joking lets you say it without risk. It also makes it easy for everyone to treat it as a joke.

n2.text:
Later that night.
Arjun: everyone's liking it though. you're overreacting, it's one photo

choices.label: "I'm not asking if it's a good photo. I'm asking you to take it down."
choices.consequence:
A few minutes pass.
Arjun: ok ok removing. didn't know you felt that strongly
choices.expert_note: You didn't debate the photo. You repeated the ask. How strongly you feel is yours to decide, not his.

choices.label: "Fine, whatever."
choices.consequence: The photo stays. You check the likes more times than you want to admit.
choices.expert_note: "Whatever" tells him it's settled. It isn't settled for you, and only you know that.

choices.label: "Can you at least ask before posting me next time?"
choices.consequence:
Arjun: who asks?? 
Arjun: ok fine
choices.expert_note: You let this one go and set the rule for the future. That's a real trade, and yours to make.

n3.text: A week later you've got a great group photo from Diwali night. Everyone looks good. Except Meher, who is laughing with her eyes completely shut. Your thumb is over Share.

choices.label: Send it to the group first: "ok to post?"
choices.consequence: You drop it in the chat and wait.
choices.expert_note: It costs a minute. It's also exactly what you wanted from Arjun.

choices.label: Post it. She looks happy.
choices.consequence: It's up. The likes start coming in.
choices.expert_note: It looks fine to you. That's the same thing Arjun said.

choices.label: Crop Meher out and post
choices.consequence: You trim the edge of the photo and post it.
choices.expert_note: You tried to protect her without asking her. Guessing can go wrong in either direction.

end_a.title: Ask first
end_a.text:
Meher: omg not that one, use the 2nd
It takes four minutes. Arjun replies "since when do we ask 😂" and then, a few days later, asks before his next post.
end_a.takeaway: Ask before you post or tag someone. It takes a minute, and it's their face.

end_b.title: Posted
end_b.text: Meher likes it. Then she DMs you: "hey can you remove it, my relatives follow me." You take it down, and think of Arjun.
end_b.takeaway: What looks fine to you can land differently for the person in it. Asking first is the only way to know.

end_c.title: Cropped
end_c.text: No harm done. Later Meher asks why she isn't in the picture, and sounds a bit left out.
end_c.takeaway: Asking beats guessing, both ways. People usually want a say, not to be left out.
